justifications.durability: the node lands no test, so the finding is guarded by nothing executable: it is a point-in-time reading of two remote hosts, and a future regression (or a migration that arrives later) would not be caught by any check in the repository. The scripts that produced it (graph_prefixes.py, remote_search.sh/.out) live under the unversioned reports directory rather than in the repository, so the method survives only as long as that directory does. This is inherent to a one-shot read-only external probe, not a defect of the work, but it is the weakest dimension.
justifications.evidence: the central claim is independently reproduced at the committed head, and the instrument that produced the negative is shown to work. I re-ran the graph census (verify_graph.out: TOTAL 1049, scored_or_discovered 781, by host jt-60sa 231 / nakasvr26 nakasvr23.iferc.org 548 / 2 external), the ssh positive control (verify_ssh_roots.log: 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes jt-60sa hostname' -> intr26-2), the web-root listing (verify_ssh_roots.log: /var/www absent, /data absent, /srv present but empty, only seven /opt system dirs), the bounded find with its positive control (verify_ssh_find.log: 'find /opt -maxdepth 8 -name qsub' -> /opt/pbs/bin/qsub, three sample filenames -> zero hits), the absence of an httpd/apache2/nginx binary and of /etc/httpd|apache2|nginx, the absence of any *twiki*/*foswiki* tree or 'pub' directory under the non-home roots, and both curl -sI calls from nakasvr26 against nakasvr23 URLs (verify_curl.log: rc=124 timeout for both) with DNS resolving nakasvr23 to 157.111.10.188. The zero-hit find is a measured absence, not a blind scan, because the identical command form locates a known-present file (/opt/pbs/bin/qsub). Weakness: I re-ran three of the ten sample filenames rather than all ten; the full run's own remote_search.out records TOTAL_HITS 0 over all ten across 15 roots. A second, minor imprecision: the fragment states '/var/www, /srv/* and /data* do not exist', but the /srv directory itself exists (empty); the operational claim (no web root, no pub tree) is correct.
